intro.data: The finale, in plain terms. You just saw an object is pinned down by the arrows into it. The Yoneda lemma turns that into a precise promise: a whole uniform family of choices — one for every arrow into A — carries no more information than a SINGLE value (the choice made on A's own identity arrow). Match each name to what it actually says. One option is a famous misconception — leave it unpaired.
intro.alchemy: The finale, in plain terms. An object is pinned down by the processes into it; the Yoneda lemma makes that a precise promise. Match each name to what it actually says. One option is a famous misconception — leave it unpaired.
intro.spellcraft: The finale, in plain terms. An essence is pinned down by the workings into it; the Yoneda lemma makes that a precise promise. Match each name to what it actually says. One option is a famous misconception — leave it unpaired.
intro.abstract: Match each concept — the representable Hom(−, A), the Yoneda lemma Nat(Hom(−,A), F) ≅ F(A), and the Yoneda embedding — to its precise statement. One offered statement is a misconception (distractor).

afterSuccess.data: That's the whole journey. You started by connecting two things with an arrow. You learned arrows compose, that some are reversible, that whole worlds map to other worlds (functors), that maps between maps are natural transformations, and that the best object for a job is a limit. The Yoneda lemma is the summit: an object is COMPLETELY determined by the arrows into it — you are who you know. Everything you built is one big web of arrows, and Yoneda says the web is all you ever needed.
afterSuccess.alchemy: That's the whole journey, summed up: a material is completely determined by the processes into it. Everything you built is one web of arrows, and Yoneda says the web is all you ever needed.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: That's the whole journey, summed up: an essence is completely determined by the workings into it. Everything you wove is one web of arrows, and Yoneda says the web is all you ever needed.
afterSuccess.abstract: The Yoneda lemma Nat(Hom(−,A), F) ≅ F(A) and its embedding C ↪ [C^op, Set] close the curriculum: an object is determined, up to isomorphism, by its representable functor. Objects are their patterns of arrows.

reveal.summary: The Yoneda lemma: Nat(Hom(−,A), F) ≅ F(A) — a natural family over the arrows into A is the same as a single element of F(A). Its embedding makes every object known, fully and faithfully, by its arrows. You are who you know.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: An interface is defined entirely by the messages it can receive — two objects answering every message identically are interchangeable.
